games.name: cairn
games.description: A CHAIN-CLEARING SOLITAIRE (Tri-Peaks/Golf-descended, reimagined as dismantling a cairn) -- the fleet's first solitaire, and a fresh shape for the thin CARD genre (was 3: squirm/deepwatch/bidstorm, none a solitaire). A cairn is a PYRAMID of runed stones (a full A-K rank ladder, four cosmetic hues); one stone is in your HAND and you take any EXPOSED stone whose rune is one step (WRAP: A<->K) above/below the hand -- it becomes the new hand and uncovers the stones it covered. Consecutive takes build a HEAT multiplier (score = 10*heat, cap 6), so a long unbroken chain is worth far more than the same stones piecemeal; when stuck you DRAW from the scree, which reseeds the hand but RESETS heat and spends one of a LIMITED draw budget. Chosen as an INVENTED idea (IDEAS.md holds only the two known-deferred entries GeoChess/photo-drop, flagged in memory don't-re-attempt-blind). TOUCH chosen ON PURPOSE (principle #23): taking one specific stone off a layout is a precise point-and-pick -- the finger IS the verb; a sensor was NOT overdue (the last sensor warble/voice-pitch shipped two days prior, and the fleet has five recent sensor games warble/brim/teeter/waft/uproar -- ~1-in-3 are sensor). THE GENERATOR IS THE CRUX: a cairn is a pure function of (mode,seed,index) and is GENERATED SOLVABLE BY CONSTRUCTION -- lay a triangular pyramid (row r has r+1 stones; (r,j) covered by (r+1,j) and (r+1,j+1); base starts exposed), pick a seeded valid REMOVAL ORDER (repeatedly remove an exposed stone -- a pyramid always has one, so generation is TOTAL and can never hang), then assign runes along that order as a +-1 walk where the first stone chains off the initial flip (a legal opening move always exists WITHOUT drawing) and each later stone is a CHAIN step (rune=hand+-1) or a DRAW-THEN-TAKE (push a scree card of rune d, stone=d+-1). That walk IS a full-clear solution stored as board.solution (the reference-solver proof); D=solution draws sets drawBudget=D+slack (scree padded so the player physically has draws up to budget). Three modes with GENUINE RULE spread (principle #14, the ENDING RULE is the axis): Ramble (one h=6/21-stone cairn, NO clock, generous scree slack 16 -- running out is a soft END not a loss, clear at your pace, score=chains+clear bonus; the calm showcase+daily), Cascade (a STREAM of small h=4/10-stone cairns vs a 60s CLOCK, clear one and the next deals instantly, a stuck cairn is swapped fresh -- a THROUGHPUT goal), Scree (one big h=7/28-stone cairn with a HARD budget slack 4 -- run out of draws with stones standing and you are BURIED, sudden death, plan-or-die). The host's mode travels FROZEN inside roundOpts; guests render state().hostOpts; modeOf() validates any id off the wire (Object.hasOwn prototype-guard). Live P2P VERSUS 2-6 is a PARALLEL SAME-SEED RACE (the proven beeline/teeter/skein/glint/hatch/warble shape, non-hostile -- nobody can touch anyone's board): every peer builds the byte-identical cairn (pure fn of mode+seed) and reaches its OWN game-over with NO board state on the wire -- only a tiny status gossip (score+cleared+cairns as progress; done+won+final score+time on finishing). HOST TRANSFER IS A PURE DISPLAY CONCERN (onHostChange wired regardless -- takeover.test proves a guest finishes with no host). Solo-first: best-score-per-mode, a UTC daily cairn, async seed-share (?seed=CODE&m=mode). Results show EVERY player's score + cleared + best-chain breakdown (principle #9 -- the knowable perfect is a full clear) with the winner star + persisted match tally. CANVAS render with juice: a taken stone FLIES to the hand with a spark + a chain pop (x2, x3..) growing with heat + a rising coin pitch; a draw slides a scree stone up and snaps heat back; clearing flashes green + bursts; buried shakes + coral-flashes + haptic; legal stones LIFT + glow amber (a ring), covered stones sit under a shadow scrim (a LIGHTNESS cue); prefers-reduced-motion aware; particle/flyer pools HARD-CAPPED. THE BALANCE SIM (principle #18, adapted for a same-seed race -> 'is the cairn fair+winnable and is reading+hoarding-draws load-bearing'), BUILT FIRST and refereed the constants: the reference solver clears 100% of every mode; a BLIND flailer almost never clears (skill gap >0.7) and scores <1/3 of a reader; SCREE'S DRAW BUDGET IS LOAD-BEARING VIA A SIGN FLIP -- the SAME careless (impatient-draw) policy NEVER buries Ramble (no lethal budget -> soft end) but buries Scree >50%, while the solver clears BOTH (0 buries); Cascade rewards throughput (solver banks many, flailer ~none); fair by construction (identical policy+seed => identical score/cleared/cairns/draws); every run bounded. games.name: skein
games.description: An UNTANGLE / graph-planarity puzzle -- the fleet's first (nothing else is a planarity/untangle toy). A web of amber beads is strung together by threads that cross in a tangle; you DRAG a bead and the crossings it was part of wink out -- a crossed thread glows THICK coral with a pulsing X where it cuts, a clean thread glows thin cyan. Untangle the whole web so nothing crosses and it settles green. THE CRUX IS THE GENERATOR: a web is a pure function of (mode,seed,index) and is PLANAR BY CONSTRUCTION so a tangle-free solution ALWAYS exists (the player is never stuck) -- lay the beads out in a spread (the SOLUTION positions), build a straight-line planar graph over them (a Euclidean minimum spanning tree, whose edges provably never cross, plus extra edges added only when they cross nothing already placed and don't run through a third bead), then SCRAMBLE the beads to random positions to make the tangle; re-scramble until it has enough crossings, with a random-order-ring fallback so generation is TOTAL and can never hang. The solution layout therefore has ZERO crossings (graph.test pins countCrossings(solution)===0 across 150 seeds x modes) -- that is the objective-completable proof. Chosen as an INVENTED idea (IDEAS.md holds only the two known-deferred entries GeoChess/photo-drop, flagged in memory don't-re-attempt-blind). TOUCH (drag) chosen ON PURPOSE (principle #23): untangling IS a direct spatial manipulation -- the finger grabs a bead and moves it, exactly the verb; a tilt/shout/shake would be strictly worse for placing a specific node, and a sensor was NOT overdue (the most recent build warble was a mic-pitch sensor game, and the fleet already has five recent sensor games uproar/teeter/waft/brim/warble). Controls: drag the nearest bead (hit radius >=44px, grab offset preserved so it doesn't jump), plus a full keyboard a11y path ([ ] or Tab pick a bead, Space/Enter grab & drop, arrows nudge a grabbed bead -- one drop = one move). The committed action is place(i,x,y): a placement that actually moves the bead counts as one move; crossings recompute; a web hitting zero solves it. Three modes with GENUINE RULE spread (principle #14, the ending RULE is the axis, not the bead count): Loom (one web, 10 beads, NO clock, NO limit -- the calm showcase + daily; score = fewest moves, par ~ one move per bead), Cascade (a STREAM of 7-bead webs against a 75s clock -- untangle one and the next deals instantly, bank as many as you can, a THROUGHPUT goal), Snarl (one big 14-bead web with a hard MOVE BUDGET of 21 -- run out before it's clean and the run is OVER, sudden death, plan-or-die). HOST TRANSFER IS A PURE DISPLAY CONCERN (onHostChange wired regardless -- takeover.test proves a guest finishes with no host). Solo-first: best-per-mode (fewest moves for Loom/Snarl, most webs for Cascade), a UTC daily web, async seed-share (?seed=CODE&m=mode). Results show EVERY player's outcome (principle #9 -- moves vs par for Loom/Snarl, webs banked for Cascade) with the winner star + persisted match tally. THE BALANCE SIM (principle #18, adapted for a same-seed race -> 'is the PUZZLE fair+winnable and is reading it LOAD-BEARING'), BUILT FIRST and refereed the constants: the reference solver (placing every bead at its known solution) untangles 100% of every mode; a BLIND flailer almost never does (skill gap >0.7 -- blind ~6% in Loom, ~0% in Snarl); SNARL'S BUDGET IS LOAD-BEARING VIA A SIGN FLIP -- the SAME sloppy policy (flail then solve) FINISHES Loom (no limit, 0% death) but DIES in Snarl (out of moves, >50% death) while the sharp solver clears both (0% death); fair by construction (identical policy+seed => identical result); every run bounded. games.name: warble
games.description: THE FLEET'S FIRST VOICE-PITCH game (principle #23): the primary input is the microphone's PITCH (voice fundamental frequency) -- uproar used mic LOUDNESS, never pitch; camera (waft), gyroscope-tilt (teeter) and accelerometer-stillness (brim) are the other sensors, so pitch was the one unused mic mechanic. Your VOICE is the controller: a mote of light flies at a height set by your pitch (hum low = fly low, whistle/sing high = fly high), a luminous cyan RIBBON weaves across a scrolling course, and keeping the mote on the ribbon scores while a clean streak raises a combo multiplier. It turns a phone into a physical, social instrument no tap game can match, and is legible in one sentence. Chosen as an INVENTED idea in the thinnest-with-a-sensor slot: the last three builds (hatch/glint/facet) were all TOUCH and the last sensor (brim) was two days prior, so a sensor was due; genre arcade (was heavy at 12 but the INPUT axis, not the genre, drove the pick). THE PURE DERIVATION (pitch.ts: detectPitch = autocorrelation with a loudness gate + a clarity gate + FIRST-PEAK selection to kill the classic octave-down subharmonic error, then pitchToHeight = a log/musical map of [100Hz,800Hz]->[0,1], then a shared HeightSmoother) is the ONE evaluator every unit test drives with SYNTHETIC TONES, so the sensor path is proven WITHOUT a mic (recovers 110-660Hz within 3%; silence/noise -> null so the mote holds); the live mic (mic.ts: getUserMedia -> AnalyserNode -> a PCM block per frame) only ever produces a NUMBER, and the game never sees audio. TOUCH IS THE FALLBACK, BUILT FIRST AND A REAL GAME: slide a finger up/down anywhere on the board (absolute vertical, so the thumb never covers the fixed-x mote nor reaches across) or hold arrow/W-S keys -- announced honestly ('No mic -- slide up and down to fly'), never a 'use your phone' wall (principle #1 outranks the sensor). PRIVACY: nothing recorded/stored/or on the wire (a P2P peer sends its SCORE, never audio), a first-run consent sheet ('Sing to fly'/'Slide instead') at the permission point, getUserMedia only from a Play TAP (0 calls on load, verified), every track stopped on teardown. Three modes with GENUINE RULE spread (principle #14, the RULE SET is the axis): Glide (a smooth forgiving wandering ribbon, TRACK a moving line, no way to die -- the calm showcase + daily), Steps (the ribbon is a staircase of DISCRETE held notes with rests between; LEAP your pitch to each rung and HOLD it steady -- a settle-and-hold game, structurally different from tracking), Thread (a NARROW ribbon strung through coral WALLS with green gaps; miss a gap and the run ENDS -- one life, sudden death). HOST TRANSFER IS A PURE DISPLAY CONCERN (onHostChange wired regardless -- takeover.test proves a guest finishes with no host). THE BALANCE SIM (principle #18, adapted for a same-seed race -> 'is reading load-bearing, is each mode's rule load-bearing, is it fair+bounded'), BUILT FIRST and refereed the constants: READING the ribbon (a tracker) CRUSHES a FLAT-height and a RANDOM non-reader in every mode (>=1.6x); THREAD'S SUDDEN DEATH IS LOAD-BEARING VIA A SIGN FLIP -- a wobble (a sloppy hand) is only a small score penalty in the forgiving Glide (tol 0.14 > the noise, ZERO deaths) but KILLS OFTEN in Thread (>50% death rate vs a precise hand's <25%), and the fractional advantage of precision is >2x larger in Thread than Glide; fair by construction (same policy+seed -> identical run); every run bounded/terminates. games.name: hatch
games.description: A PICROSS / NONOGRAM logic-paint puzzle -- the fleet's first deduction-grid game (nothing else is a logic puzzle you solve by reading numeric clues). A grid hides a picture; each row/column lists the lengths of its runs of filled squares in order (3 1 = three, a gap, one); you deduce which squares must be filled and reveal the picture. THE COMMITTED ACTION IS THE FILL: a MARK (X) is a free reversible note, but filling a square that's truly EMPTY is a MISTAKE (it snaps to a mark and costs you) -- so certainty is the skill, guessing is punished. Chosen as an INVENTED idea (IDEAS.md holds only the two known-deferred entries GeoChess/photo-drop, flagged in memory don't-re-attempt-blind: GeoChess's mechanic is unconfirmable autonomously + its name needs the author's permission, photo-drop is a CC0-photo copyright risk). TOUCH chosen ON PURPOSE (principle #23): a deliberate cell-by-cell deduction puzzle wants a precise finger painting specific squares, not a tilt/shout; a sensor was NOT overdue (the last sensor build brim/accelerometer shipped the day before; waft/camera + teeter/gyro are recent -- ~1-in-3 are sensor). THE GENERATOR IS THE CRUX: a board is a pure function of (mode,seed) and is generated SOLVABLE-BY-LOGIC (line-solvable => no guessing) and UNIQUE (line-solvable => unique) BY CONSTRUCTION -- draw a random bitmap at the mode's density, compute clues, run a LINE SOLVER (force any cell filled/empty in EVERY placement of a line's clue consistent with knowns, to a fixpoint); accept the first line-solvable candidate else re-draw from a sub-seed (budget 800), with a guaranteed line-solvable STRIPES fallback making generation TOTAL so a daily seed can never crash/hang (measured: 10x10 accepts in avg 1.7 attempts, 0 fallbacks across the sweep, ~0.2ms/board). The line solver doubles as generator + uniqueness proof + the mechanism audit's independent clue check. Controls: TAP to fill, DRAG to paint a run (a fill-drag stops on the first mistake so a drag can't rack up strikes), a big Fill/Mark toggle in the thumb zone, plus a full keyboard scheme (arrows move a cursor, Space fills, X marks). CANVAS render with juice: fill pops+particles, mistake shake+red flash+haptics, line-done clue DIMMING with a strikethrough (a shape cue, not colour), a completion light-sweep, procedural audio. games.name: waft
games.description: THE FLEET'S FIRST CAMERA GAME (principle #23 -- every prior game is finger-on-glass, gyroscope, or voice; the camera is the one sensor never used). Fireflies drift into a grid of squares over a faint, mirrored camera view and glow, then fade; you WAVE YOUR HAND in front of the camera, over a firefly's square, and the camera senses per-zone MOTION and bursts it into sparks. Clean quick catches build a COMBO that multiplies each catch; letting one fade OR waving over an empty square resets the combo, so precision is the whole game (that whiff-breaks-combo rule was the balance sim's fix -- see below). In Sting mode wasps hide among the fireflies: wave over one and you're stung (points lost, combo broken). The mechanic is 'a sensor reading (per-zone frame-difference motion) compared against a threshold' -- no ML, no library, just pixel deltas, fully self-contained and offline. TOUCH IS THE FALLBACK, BUILT FIRST AND A REAL GAME: a missing/denied/absent camera lands the player in a TAP whack-a-mole (tap a firefly to catch it; desktop clicks or number keys 1-9), announced honestly ('No camera -- tap the fireflies'), never a 'use your phone' wall (principle #1 outranks the sensor). THE PURE DERIVATION (motion.ts frameDiffZones: two grayscale frames -> per-zone mean |delta| normalized 0..1) is the unit-tested core, so the sensor path is proven WITHOUT a real camera; the live camera source downsamples the MIRRORED video to a tiny grayscale buffer and hands it here, and the game never sees a pixel. PRIVACY IS LOAD-BEARING AND HONEST: frames are diffed in-place and discarded, only the derived per-zone energy NUMBER is used, NOTHING (never a video frame) is recorded/stored/or put on the P2P wire, permission is requested from the Play TAP not on load (verified: 0 getUserMedia calls on load), a first-time disclosure sheet with a Use-camera/Use-taps choice appears at the permission point, and every track is stopped at teardown (verified in-browser: a granted track went live->ended on quit, so the OS camera indicator goes out). Three modes with GENUINE spread (principle #14, the RULE SET/grid is the axis): Meadow (2x3, 60s, calm combo-builder), Swarm (3x3, faster shorter-lived fireflies, 90s -- more ground to cover), Sting (2x3, ~32% wasps to AVOID, 75s -- a selective game, structurally different). The host's mode travels FROZEN inside roundOpts; guests render the gossiped choice. Live P2P VERSUS 2-6 is a PARALLEL SAME-SEED RACE (the proven beeline/outsize/teeter shape): every peer catches on its OWN copy of the byte-identical seeded firefly SCHEDULE (a pure function of mode+seed; per-zone independent timelines guarantee AT MOST ONE alive mote per zone, so a swat is unambiguous) and reaches its OWN game-over (the clock) with NO game state on the wire -- only a tiny status gossip (score, catches, best combo, done), NEVER a camera image. HOST TRANSFER IS A PURE DISPLAY CONCERN (onHostChange wired regardless). Solo-first: endless best-per-mode, a UTC daily swarm, async seed-share (?seed=CODE&m=mode). Results show EVERY player's score + catches/perfect + best combo (principle #9) with the knowable 'caught X/Y fireflies' so everyone sees what they missed. THE BALANCE SIM (principle #18, adapted for a same-seed race -> the framing is 'is the swarm fair+winnable and is skill LOAD-BEARING'), BUILT FIRST, REFEREED AND OVERRULED THE DESIGN: the first pass had a blind random MASHER tying a perfect reader EXACTLY (7090 vs 7090 in Meadow) because with few zones + long firefly life + a per-zone cooldown, random swatting caught everything AND maxed the combo just like careful play -- the signature mechanic was NOT load-bearing (the negative-gap lesson). THE FIX both makes reading load-bearing AND deepens the game: a WHIFF (waving over an empty square) breaks the combo, the classic keep-your-streak-clean arcade rule -- now a masher whiffs ~45% and its combo never climbs while a careful reader keeps the chain, so the reader vastly out-scores the masher in every mode; and in Sting a bot BLIND to wasps (waves at everything) scores WORSE than one that avoids them (the negative gap that proves the avoid rule), while in the wasp-free modes that same difference is exactly zero (the rule is inert where it shouldn't apply). MUTATION-VERIFIED: reverting the whiff fix turns BOTH balance AND the mechanism audit red; flipping the fly/wasp resolution turns them red; both revert clean. Also asserts: every board winnable (worst reader catch-fraction >0.75, median >0.9), identical bots on one seed score IDENTICALLY (fair by construction), every run terminates, the daily changes day to day. THE MECHANISM AUDIT (principle #21, solo-vs-system): an INDEPENDENT re-derivation over the sim's event stream (its OWN scoring constants, NOT imported from the game -- the 'audit must not import game math' lesson) confirms at ZERO tolerance across 3 modes that every catch was a live firefly in that zone, every sting a live wasp, conservation (catches+misses == fireflies), whiffs never ADD score (only their combo-reset lowers later catches, which the replay models), and the independent score matches the engine EXACTLY -- mutation-verified with planted bad events (a wasp counted as a catch, a catch after the fade, a double-resolve) each caught. CONTRAST (principle #22): the camera feed is arbitrary pixels, so it's drawn at a capped CAMERA_ALPHA=0.18 that makes the LIGHTEST possible play-surface pixel (white camera pixel over the board) no lighter than PALETTE.bgWorst -- a genuine analytic bound PROVEN in the test (composite(white,board,0.18) luminance <= bgWorst). Every meaningful colour (firefly #ffd24a, its core, the wasp #ff6b57, the cyan motion pulse, the spark) clears 3:1 on bgWorst (and the darker board/panels); text 4.5:1; the IN-BROWSER PIXEL PROBE agreed (a firefly painted as EXACTLY #ffd24a, 12.47:1 vs an empty cell -- painted == declared). Colour-blind safe by SHAPE: a firefly is a round glow, a wasp a spiky striped diamond. 136 tests. SENSOR Part C: a synthetic motion feed drove injected-energy -> catch -> score end-to-end through the REAL active source; the fallback tap/click path verified per mode; permission on-tap-not-on-load, denied->fallback, track live->ended on teardown all confirmed in-browser; a real-device hand-wave check is NOT possible in this pipeline (stated plainly). games.name: wordloom
games.description: A word game about BUILDING the grid, not reading it (mechanically distinct from the fleet's other two word games: cipher-clash finds words in a fixed Boggle grid, unstrung cuts words from a strand). Letters arrive one at a time from a deterministic seeded stream; you drop each into an empty square you cannot later move; when the grid is full every ROW and COLUMN scores its best contiguous 3+ word (longest valid run), scored as (sum of Scrabble-ish tile values) x a STEEP length multiplier (3:1, 4:1.6, 5:2.4, 6:3.4) so long words are the prize. The tension is that each square is a two-axis bet (a row AND a column at once), and words light up LIVE as you weave them (amber weft underline for a row, teal warp side-bar for a column, violet ring for a diagonal). Chosen as an invented idea in the thinnest buildable genre (word=2 before this) since IDEAS.md holds only the two known-deferred entries (GeoChess unconfirmable; photo-drop a CC0-photo copyright risk) flagged in memory as don't-re-attempt-blind. TOUCH chosen ON PURPOSE (principle #23): a deliberate spatial placement puzzle wants a finger weighing two crossing words, not a sensor; the cadence agrees (the immediately-preceding build teeter was the gyroscope sensor build, so a touch build is due). THE CURATED DICTIONARY (the word-game make-or-break lesson): scripts/gen-dictionary.mjs pulls SCOWL frequency bands via wordlist-english with length-scaled leniency (len3<=band35 ... len6<=60), only lengths 3-6 (the longest scoring line is 6) -> 15,839 everyday words, ~38KB gz, inlined via ?raw offline; junk (NOM/GOS/QAT) rejected, real inflections + long words (CATS/PLAYED/ABSEIL/QUARTZ) accepted, pinned by dict.test.ts. Three modes with GENUINE spread (principle #14, the RULE is the axis): Weave (5x5, BLIND one-at-a-time, rows+cols), Sluice (5x5, you see a QUEUE of the next 3 and place ANY of them in any order -> planning over luck), Deluge (6x6, blind, rows+cols AND both main diagonals -> the centre cells are triple-weighted). The host's mode travels FROZEN inside roundOpts; guests see the gossiped choice. Live P2P VERSUS 2-6 is a PARALLEL SAME-SEED RACE (the proven beeline/outsize/teeter shape): every peer weaves its OWN grid from the byte-identical seeded stream and reaches its OWN game-over (grid full / round-timer) with NO game state on the wire -- only a tiny status gossip (score, placed, done) plus the final grid ONCE on finishing so results show everyone's board (principle #9). THE BALANCE/SOLVABILITY SIM (principle #18, adapted -- a same-seed race has no seats/shared-board/snowball, so the framing is the PUZZLE being fair), BUILT FIRST and it set the tuning: a word-knowing greedy placer far outscores a random one every mode (mechanic load-bearing); SLUICE'S QUEUE IS LOAD-BEARING -- a placer USING the 3-letter look-ahead beats the same placer forced to place the front letter (the mechanic goes NEGATIVE when disabled, the negative-gap-proves-a-mechanic test); DELUGE'S DIAGONALS actually fire; NO dead boards (the baseline set vowelRatio to 0.44, since 0.40 left ~1% of boards where even greedy found no word); identical bots on one seed finish IDENTICAL (the race is fair by construction). CONTRAST (principle #22): DOM tiles so the palette constants ARE the paint; the initial palette FAILED the probe (empty-cell-vs-board 1.45, thread-vs-board low) and was reworked to a darker board with GAP-BASED gridlines and scoring markers drawn ON the dark tile -- every meaningful colour now >=3:1 with margin, and the IN-BROWSER DOM PROBE agreed (painted == declared: tile #33291f 3.72:1 vs board, weft #d47b12 4.49:1, glyph 12.52:1); colour-blind safe via distinct SHAPES (underline/side-bar/ring), not colour alone. 171 tests. games.name: squirm
games.description: A face-to-face bluffing card game built from the IDEAS.md Cockroach-Poker-shaped line (mechanic not identity: original name, original cute-grotesque procedural SVG critters, original copy — no reference to the source). THE SIGNATURE ACT: on your turn you slide ONE card from your hand FACE-DOWN to a rival and DECLARE a critter ('a spider') — true or a bald-faced lie, your choice. The receiver resolves it three ways, which is the whole game: BELIEVE (call it true), CALL BLUFF (call it a lie), or — the social twist — PEEK & PASS it on to a third player with a fresh claim of their own. When a card is finally challenged and revealed, whoever GUESSED WRONG takes it face-up into their menagerie; you LOSE the instant you collect the threshold of any one critter (4, or 3 in Swarm). The pressure is read-the-PERSON not read-the-board: a card can travel the whole table, the danger is targeted (everyone piles claims on whoever's already sitting on three spiders), a 'believe' can be the trap and a 'call bluff' can hand you the very card you feared. THE FLEET'S FIRST GENUINELY HOST-AUTHORITATIVE HIDDEN-INFO GAME (all the recent P2P games were same-seed parallel races); modelled on nightwire's Session: the host holds the shuffled deck + every hand's true identities + each in-flight card's true face, gossips ONLY public state (whose turn, hand COUNTS, face-up menageries, the in-flight card's DECLARED type + pass trail + who peeked — never the true face until reveal), and privately deals each peer its own hand via a targeted send. HOST TRANSFER is fully recoverable here precisely because Cockroach-Poker deals the WHOLE deck into hands (NO draw pile to lose) and each hand's owner keeps it locally: the promoted peer rebuilds public state from its last snapshot, REWINDS any in-flight card to its origin (a seer who still knows its type), and asks every survivor to re-attest their own hand (htake/hgive channels) — proven end-to-end by takeover.test.ts (a 3-Session in-memory wire promotes the min-id survivor, recovers both hands, and drives the game to over) AND live (closing the host tab → the survivor was promoted, did NOT freeze). SOLO-FIRST (principle #1): instantly playable vs 3 bots with distinct, learnable bluffing personalities (Honest Ada lieRate .24, Sly Cove .56, Reckless Bo, Cagey Wren...) whose caught-lie history is shown under each name as a tell; solo carries the single-player mode since the game needs 3+ to shine (2 is a valid lighter believe/doubt duel — peek auto-disables with no third target). Live P2P 2-6, minPlayers 2 so a friend-duel + the 2-tab smoke both work. Touch chosen ON PURPOSE (principle #23): a read-the-person card game is select-a-card/pick-a-target/pick-a-claim/believe-or-doubt — a sensor would hurt it (the point is watching faces, and #23 forbids audio/video on the wire); it's a QUEUE idea so the queue takes priority over the sensor pull (flagged: last sensor game uproar was 5 builds ago, a sensor build still due next NON-queue run). Three modes with GENUINE spread (principle #14): Parlour (6 critters, out at 4, peek ON — the classic travel-the-table read), Snap (5 critters, out at 4, peek OFF so the card never travels — a fast direct believe/doubt duel, a structurally different game), Swarm (4 critters, out at THREE, peek ON — danger everywhere, the table gangs up fast). THE BALANCE SIM (principle #18, adapted for a hidden-info bluffer: seat fairness + no-dominant-rote + no-death-sentence-critter + termination), BUILT FIRST, refereed the design and OVERRULED it FOUR times: (1) ALWAYS-PEEK DOMINATED (53% in parlour, 32% swarm) because peek was a free escape from the lethal card — fixed with a per-round PEEK BUDGET (1 in parlour/swarm) making it a spendable resource, mutation-verified (budget 99 → always-peek jumps to 46%/42%); (2) a SEAT-0 WIN BIAS at 4p that was really the RANKING TIE-BREAK on seat index (the ballast 'ties → seat 0' lesson) — fixed with a SEED-DERIVED tie key, mutation-verified (seat-index tie-break turns 4p seat fairness red); (3) a 90% FORFEIT RATE in 4p Snap (the signature 'collect N' loss barely fired because a fixed deck went thin at higher player counts and hands depleted first) — fixed by SCALING copies with player count (copiesBase+copiesPerPlayer*n), dropping forfeits to ~0% at every count, mutation-verified; (4) a 'spider death-sentence' (33% of losses) that was a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT in the test's byType tie-break firing on forfeits — the true kill-type (from the eliminate event) is uniform across critters. Also randomised the first giver from the seed (seat 0 no longer always opens). Final: every seat within ~5 of chance at 3p/4p across all modes, no rote script (always-truth/bluff/peek) beats the balanced reader (bluff-always is a dismal 11-16%, proving the read is load-bearing), losses even across critters, all games terminate (structural: cards only move hand→menagerie so hands strictly shrink). THE MECHANISM AUDIT (principle #21): the resolution rule (RIGHT receiver → giver keeps it; WRONG → receiver takes it) is RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY over the event stream at ZERO tolerance across 200 seeded games x 3 modes (0 mis-resolutions, 0 wrong takers, 0 illegal peeks in Snap, engine's take-count matches an independent tally), never importing the game's own resolution — MUTATION-VERIFIED (flipping receiverCorrect turns mechanism 3/3 + game 6/6 red). CONTRAST (principle #22): every critter is drawn on the cream card and held >=3:1 vs it (worst grub 4.53:1), meaning colours (danger ring, actor/target highlights, peek) >=3:1 on the dark surfaces, text >=4.5:1; critters are DOM SVG so the constants ARE the paint — the in-browser probe confirmed chip bg == #f4ebe0 and grub fill == #2c7a2f. Colour-blind safe: each critter has a UNIQUE silhouette, colour is a redundant cue. TWO REAL BUGS the live 2-tab smoke caught that no unit test could: (a) the SURVIVOR of a 2-player host-leave was marked the LOSER ('You collected one too many') by endIfDone's pickWorst — fixed so a departure-collapse is a WALKOVER (the last player standing WINS, a departed seat is the nominal loser); (b) BOTH PEERS WERE NAMED 'You' (playerName defaulted to 'You') — fixed with a distinct random handle per device (Heron-98, Newt-50...). Also a peek-targetable bug caught in the first solo browser pass (targets weren't highlighted during peek-pass because the highlight was gated on selCard!=null which is null mid-peek). 148 tests. Verified in a real browser at a true 375x812 for ALL THREE modes on localhost AND the LIVE production https URL (deploy green, cert approved on the FIRST poll, Pages CNAME cycled ONCE): the full solo loop played through (give→believe/bluff, peek→reveal 'you saw: Grub'→pass with a lie, correct call registering, the tell 'Sly Cove 1 lie 100%' appearing) to a results screen showing EVERY player's menagerie (principle #9 — winner #1 'clean slate', loser OUT with the killing 3-roach pile in a red ring); zero horizontal overflow, >=44px targets, no stray overlay, footer hidden mid-round, zero console errors; AND at a WIDE 1280px desktop (centred column, no sprawl, no slivers — the viewport axis outsize failed). FULL two-peer P2P smoke test passed on localhost against the real relay (byte-identical build): typed LOWER-CASE code '28hu' normalising to 28HU and resolving to the same room; mesh 2/6; HOST STICKINESS (creator kept HOST, joiner adopted as guest); the QR dark-on-light encoding the invite LINK (not the bare code) with 'Scan to join room 28HU', not clipped; IN-SYNC bidirectional play (a Spider claim propagating host↔guest); HOST-LEAVE → the survivor promoted, NOT frozen, winning by WALKOVER; LIVE REMATCH → both peers in a fresh Round 2 seeing each other (mesh alive, one host), a fresh board, and a PERSISTED match tally; distinct player handles. Rematch/no-deadlock/host-election/net-lifecycle/room-code/takeover are also covered by the green, mutation-verified automated tests.

games.name: teeter
games.description: The fleet's FIRST TILT game (principle #23): the primary input is the GYROSCOPE — you hold the phone flat, tilt it, and a marble rolls downhill under real momentum through a top-down maze to a glowing exit; score is TIME. Chosen as a NON-QUEUE sensor build because the queue's two remaining ideas stay blocked (GeoChess — rules unconfirmable, geochess.org serves only a placeholder; photo-drop — hinges on ~150 verifiably-CC0 geotagged photos, a copyright risk that can't be de-risked unattended) and the last sensor game (uproar, voice) was 5 builds ago with multiple entries flagging a sensor build was overdue. Tilt chosen ON PURPOSE: rolling a ball is the canonical thing a tilt sensor does; a 'drag where to go' would put the thumb over the very ball being steered (principle #19's banned reach-across). NOTE: an incomplete 'squirm' (a hidden-info bluff CARD game, a queue idea) was left ~40% done by a stalled earlier run today (no main.ts/render/CSS, 1 of ~15 tests, no repo) — its idea was consumed from IDEAS.md but never shipped; teeter was built fresh instead (finishing squirm's complex hidden-info netcode from unfamiliar partial code was higher-risk, and the fleet is card-heavy). squirm's plan.md + src remain for a future resume. THE SENSOR ARCHITECTURE (principle #23): a PURE derivation `tiltFromOrientation({beta,gamma},neutral,{screenAngle})` → gravity vector, unit-tested hard (calibration, dead-zone, clamp, screen-orientation rotation) since automation can't tilt a phone; a per-round NEUTRAL calibration so 'level' is wherever you hold it; and ONE TiltSource interface with three implementations (gyro / engine floating joystick / arrow-keys) all feeding the SAME deterministic physics. The FALLBACK is built first and is a real game: a missing/denied gyro lands in the joystick game with an honest 'No tilt sensor — drag anywhere to steer' announce, never a wall; iOS permission is requested from the Play tap; gyro exposes only orientation angles (no stream, no camera/mic, nothing to record or stop at teardown). THE PHYSICS is a hand-rolled deterministic circle-in-grid integrator: fixed 120Hz substeps, no Math.random, speed cap MAX_V*SUB_DT (0.075) << BALL_R (0.34) so the marble can NEVER tunnel a wall in one substep (asserted structurally + mutation-verified). Maze is a pure function of (mode,seed) — THE WHOLE P2P-SYNC SURFACE — a randomized-DFS perfect maze, braided for route choice, with pits placed OFF a chosen shortest start→exit path and gems only on pit-avoiding-reachable cells, so solvability is BY CONSTRUCTION. Three modes with real spread (principle #14, the RULE SET is the axis): Dash (small 8x8, no hazards — a pure racing line, 60s), Sinkhole (12x12 with 12 pits that respawn you at the start, 90s), Scatter (14x14, collect all 5 gems then the exit opens, 9 pits, 150s). Live P2P VERSUS 2-6 is a PARALLEL SAME-SEED RACE (the proven beeline/landbridge/outsize/ballast shape): each peer rolls its OWN marble on the byte-identical maze and reaches its OWN game-over (reach the exit / clock out) with NO ball state on the wire — only a tiny status gossip (gems left, falls, and on finishing: done/won/time). HOST TRANSFER IS A PURE DISPLAY CONCERN (onHostChange wired regardless). Solo-first: endless best-time (persisted per mode), a UTC daily maze, async seed-share (?seed=CODE&m=mode deep-link). Results show EVERY player's time + the fastest (principle #9), with a persisted match tally. THE BALANCE/SOLVABILITY SIM (principle #18, adapted for a same-seed race — no seat order/shared board/snowball, so the framing is the PUZZLE being fair): built FIRST and refereed the constants — a maze-reading bot completes 100% of boards in every mode comfortably inside the limit (dash median 15s/60, sinkhole 29s/90, scatter 64s/150), a blind wanderer almost never does (skill gap >0.7 → mechanic load-bearing), identical bots on the same seed finish in the IDENTICAL time (the race is fair by construction), every run terminates. games.name: amble
games.description: An unhurried travel game built from the IDEAS.md 'Tokaido'-shaped line (mechanic not identity: original name, original procedural woodblock art — flat colour planes, a dark ink road winding down warm paper — no reference to the source). The signature rule is the whole game: you move a traveller FORWARD to any open stop on a one-way road, take its little reward, and then the turn passes to WHOEVER IS NOW FURTHEST BEHIND — so a short hop keeps you at the back for another turn soon, while a long leap grabs a coveted distant stop before a rival can but then sits you idle while everyone behind mops up everything you skipped. No dice, no combat, no hidden info. Four set-collection routes: commit ONE view deep (only your deepest panorama scores, capped, so depth beats breadth), collect a souvenir SPREAD (distinct kinds only — variety, not volume), grind springs (small flat + a most-springs majority), and rush the first-come INN menu (arrive first, eat the value-8 dish; last eats the 1). THE BALANCE SIM, BUILT FIRST, CAUGHT THE IDEA'S OWN BALANCE FLAG (a) AND OVERRULED THE DESIGN: with no cap on stops, 'furthest-behind moves next' is so strong a catch-up device that ALWAYS TAKING THE SHORTEST HOP WINS 100% (an ambler took 41 landings to a leaper's 6, filling every bucket the leaper couldn't) — the road's central decision was fake. Capping the SCORING (single deepest view, distinct-only souvenirs, diminishing springs, steep inn gradient) fixed the leader-decided-early curve but did NOTHING to ambling dominance, because the dawdler still filled the capped buckets while the leaper, with far fewer turns, could not. The real fix is a CLAIM BUDGET: every traveller may claim the SAME number of open-road stops (inns are free/mandatory), so turn ORDER matters and turn COUNT does not, and the only decision is which stops to spend claims on — rush far for a prize (handing the turn to those behind) or take the sure thing near. A second bug hid inside it: clonePlayer dropped the new `claims` field, so `NaN >= budget` never fired and the budget silently didn't exist (the ambler still had 18 claims to the budget's 9); fixed and MUTATION-VERIFIED (reverting the budget-through-clones makes ambling dominate again and the balance test goes red in all three modes). Final at n=60/cell replicated across families (4p seat arm at n=200): no pure style dominates (adaptive 'balanced' beats both extremes; rushing is correct WHEN the right stop is far, so it is not strictly dominated — flag a satisfied); skill beats random 97-99%; every 4p seat lands 22-30% at n=400 (an 8% seat at n=60 was pure sampling noise — the 'sample size is a finding' lesson); leader at 30% of the road wins 43-54% (near chance) rising to 84-98% at 85% (that curve IS the drama); blowouts bounded, every run terminates. LOCKSTEP netcode: no randomness in play, no hidden info (road, stops, inn menus are pure functions of the seed), so a move is just [to,dish] and every peer re-simulates — NO board state crosses the wire, nothing to desync, host transfer a display concern. Contrast (principle #22): every bright waypoint disc >=3:1 on the dark road AND each carries a distinct ICON, so colour-blindness is covered. Three modes with real spread (principle #14): Towpath (short/spring-heavy — end races decide it), Long Road (long/vista-market-rich — deep panoramas and inn timing), Wayward (views SCATTERED per seed — a routing puzzle that never learns twice). TWO REAL BUGS the live in-browser pass caught that nothing else could: the INN MEAL MENU opened on pointerup then CLOSED on the following synthesized click landing on the fresh backdrop (invisible to unit tests, fatal on real touch) — fixed with a short arm-guard; and REPAINTING THE LOBBY ON EVERY NET EVENT rebuilt it, wiping the engine's qrOpen sticky state (the QR yanked off screen mid-scan — the ballast/turntide 'rebuilding-engine-view-drops-state' lesson) — fixed to repaint() in place, plus moved the room-level rounds/move-channel teardown out of the per-screen teardown() (it was destroying them the instant a round started, freezing the board) and added a frame-loop self-heal so visuals can never freeze on a missed repaint. 214 tests.
